independent_audit.format_contract: direct np.load(path, mmap_mode='r', allow_pickle=False) of standard NPY files; exact fixed shapes, finite values, complete completion.json required
all_step_requirements: QP damage and delta_max for monotonicity/first failure
QP cohesive/contact opening and traction for work, contact energy, failure and post-failure checks
patch displacement every step for independently rebuilt external work
independent_audit.node_stride_effect: stride 1 enables strict full-step central-difference and internal/external work identities; stride 50 only permits sampled node-state reconstruction and is explicitly reported as such
independent_audit.streaming_risk: audit currently uses full-history NumPy expressions including np.diff, trapezoid integration, contact norms and comparisons; an NPZ reader alone would decompress/copy chunks and old audit expressions can still materialize large arrays. A chunk-aware audit iterator/reduction is required for bounded peak RAM.

fragment_extraction.format_contract: direct NPY memmaps for node_state, damage, traction, opening, contact_traction, and direct node_saved_steps NPY
must_preserve: all-step damage and traction to establish first joint full-damage/zero-traction frame and continued failure gate
all saved node snapshots after joint failure for gap/separation witness
final node displacement/velocity and final QP damage/traction/opening/contact state for output extraction
fragment_extraction.compatibility_risk: both exporters require existing individual NPY paths and receipt coverage; compressed chunks need a reader/exporter adaptation or a verified lazy compatibility layer. Reconstructing monolithic arrays would recreate peak-disk pressure.

receipt_and_checkpoint.current: receipt.json inventories and hashes every file; audit rejects extra/missing files. Full-size NPY memmaps are pre-sized before step 0 and flushed every flush_stride frames (case stride 250), then checkpoint.json is written; finally flush occurs even on failure.
receipt_and_checkpoint.risk: a pre-sized NPY tail is zero-filled/unwritten after a crash; checkpoint/result/completion must be used to reject incomplete histories. write_json writes directly, so current checkpoint JSON is not itself an atomic commit record.
receipt_and_checkpoint.chunk_design: publish each chunk via temp file, flush+fsync, atomic rename, then atomically replace a manifest that records contiguous committed frame range, node steps, exact shapes/dtypes, byte count and SHA-256. Only a COMPLETE manifest with exact expected coverage can pass an independent audit; partial prefixes are diagnostic only and do not imply solver restartability.

chunk_design.compressed_size_reason: No full trajectory exists; the zero-step preflight has no evolved history. Lossless deflate output cannot be forecast from mesh counts or synthetic data.

forecast_scope.current_history_specs: 11 float64 arrays sampled every solver step plus node_state float64 at the declared stride; excludes the small QP first-full-damage summary and runtime JSON/control files.

excluded_qp_failure_summary.consumer: independent auditor recomputes and compares the per-QP full-damage step

forecast_scope.run_budget_note: The prior 2,000,000-byte safety allowance covers this small summary and JSON/control outputs, but its forecast is not a complete per-file inventory of a completed evolution run. Filesystem allocation units are also excluded.

design_recommendation.bounded_next_step: Keep float64 and every QP value at every time step. Prototype chunked NumPy storage behind a versioned manifest; first preserve the current NPY layout as a legacy read contract. The tiny NPZ prototype verifies lossless chunks/commit markers but does not estimate vessel-data compression.
design_recommendation.raw_npy_chunk_storage_effect: recovery/commit granularity and bounded read blocks improve; logical numeric storage remains essentially the same as current full NPY arrays. It is not a fix for the 64 MiB cap.
design_recommendation.lossless_compressed_npz_effect: may reduce bytes, but exact real size and runtime are unknowable before a representative trajectory. Retain raw-size allocation as the safe forecast until the first actual chunk is measured and the entire run can be budgeted.

suggested_initial_chunk_sizes.reason: keeps combined raw QP/diagnostic and node-state payload below 64 MiB per chunk (about 59.0 MiB and 47.7 MiB respectively), before small headers

prohibited_savings_for_this_review: treating compression ratios from synthetic arrays as real-history estimates

tiny_prototype.scope: synthetic float64 arrays only; no native model or solver evolution
